Hi OP. I was waiting for you to post this to say something that has been in my mind since we all started talking about poem readings here, about a week ago.

On the first days of this year I mentioned that I had a feeling this would be v/shortpoems' year (read it here). When I said that I was hoping that more people would join the sub and we would have more posts and quality discussion here.

I couldn't, in my wildest dreams imagine that before the end of February we would be having reading sessions, a very promising new mod, plenty of OCs and so much going on around here. With this in mind I am now allowing myself to hope that this won't be the year for v/shortpoems but actually the start of something bigger and a lot more lasting than a calendar year :) Can you guys imagine where we will be by December if good news such as these just keep on coming?

For all of this I thank the Great Leader and founder @agitprop who has also been keeping the sub alive with great content every day or mostly - I'm not sure where it comes from but I know for sure I'm enjoying them.

As a final but not any less important note but perhaps more egotistical: as a poet it's sublime to see such beautiful voices and talented minds reading something of mine. I don't share all of my poems with my friends - and even when I do they're not offering to read them for me, even more so because we don't speak English around here. I wonder how many poets - professional or amateur, have died without knowing how their pieces sounded to other people. This may sound exaggerated, but I'm not sure it really is...

I just want you to know this means a lot to me. Today and yesterday are certainly the highest points of my "career" so far as a poet and it feels good to - you know, at the very least know for sure that I'm not writing complete gibberish and that my meaning, even if cryptic, is capable of making it out of the poem and into the reader's head clearly. I know this to be true because otherwise your readings wouldn't be nearly as beautiful and touching as they are, as perfect as I could have wished for.

I can't think of better ways to spend a single minute than listening to your voices :) goes to show size really doesn't matter!

I'm making this long post to @Dashippy as well (and the sub community as a whole), we'll probably be posting his reading very soon as well! I'd be honored if you guys want to read some more of my stuff, besides other poems here - just let me know and I'll send more material your way!

Common salt is a mineral composed primarily of sodium chloride (NaCl), a chemical compound belonging to the larger class of salts; salt in its natural form as a crystalline mineral is known as rock salt or halite. Salt is present in vast quantities in seawater, where it is the main mineral constituent; the open ocean has about 35 grams (1.2 oz) of solids per litre, a salinity of 3.5%. Salt is essential for animal life, and saltiness is one of the basic human tastes. The tissues of animals contain larger quantities of salt than do plant tissues; therefore the typical diets of nomads who subsist on their flocks and herds require little or no added salt, whereas cereal-based diets require supplementation. Salt is one of the oldest and most ubiquitous of food seasonings, and salting is an important method of food preservation.
